mechanism: RESET-anchored episodic retry on an interactive LLM game agent (ARC-AGI-3, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 served via vLLM, ARC3-Inference harness). A stuck-detector (H=4 turns with no level progress) arms a retry_mode; while armed, the agent may call a newly exposed attempt(actions) helper that runs up to K=5 short episodes inside ONE turn, each terminated by an environment RESET that returns the level to its start frame (cap 40 episodes/game). The affordance is announced to the model ONLY by adding a paragraph to the Python tool's description string (_PYTHON_TOOL_DESCRIPTION). Rationale for the arm: the game score formula 100*k(k+1)/(N(N+1)) makes extra ACTIONS nearly free above the operating point (measured epsilon 0.17), so buying level-completions with action volume should be positive-EV.
summary: The intervention was delivered and certified but the model would not use it. The stuck-trigger fired on 24/25 games (pre-registered bar >=15/25) and all three boot markers certified, yet only 75 of 699 armed turns (10.7%) called attempt() against a pre-registered kill line of 25%. The ceiling on the tightest defensible denominator (408 acting turns) is 18.4%, so the gate fails on every reading. Verdict class DELIVERY FAILURE (CERTIFIED-DELIVERED-NOT-USED): no lc verdict is licensed and seed 2 is refused by the prereg's own re-scope-never-re-read clause. Descriptively lc 24 vs floor 28 at n=1 MDE 11.1 -- indistinguishable, and not the basis of the verdict.
lesson: When your mechanism is 'tell the model it MAY do X', the binding constraint is the model's PREFERENCE, not the plumbing -- and you can and should pre-measure it. This arm pre-measured whether its trigger would FIRE (on retained artifacts, predicted 19/25, observed 24/25 -- excellent) but had no pre-measurement of whether the model would USE the affordance once fired, and that is exactly where it died. Pre-register a USE-rate gate estimated from retained transcripts BEFORE building. Second, diagnose the failure correctly before repairing: 24 of 106 attempt() calls arrived on UNARMED turns, i.e. the model knew the affordance existed and reached for it unprompted, so this is a preference failure, not a discovery failure, and making the tool more prominent is the wrong fix. Third and most transferable: an affordance advertised only inside a tool-call schema or tool description is not advertised -- this is now the third independent confirmation in one campaign (96.3% delivery/no behaviour change; 1.3% vs a 30% bar; 10.7% vs a 25% bar).
why_informative: Delivery is not in doubt here, which is what makes this null worth serving. Unlike the campaign's two earlier delivery failures, this arm carried a job-directory USE instrument that AST-counts calls per game and flushes to disk independently of the log, so the use-rate was measurable even before the kernel log was retrieved; and the patch, boot invariant and vehicle were all certified from markers. The null therefore rules OUT the pipe (patch applied, trigger armed, affordance present, environment semantics verified on the real simulator) and rules IN the agent's policy. It bounds a whole family: the resource-inversion argument for retry remains arithmetically sound and untested, because the agent never exercised it enough to test it. Anyone attempting agent-affordance interventions on a frontier-ish open-weights model should expect single-digit-to-low-teens uptake from a tool-description announcement and budget a stronger delivery channel or an obligatory (non-optional) code path.

robustness: D2 recomputed under both available denominators (armed turn-events 699 and acting turns 408); fails both. Certification re-run after repairing an incomplete artifact download (see instrument_incidents) and passed on all six required markers. Scorer duck_eval/p2/p2_score.py carries a 33/33 selftest including a healthy positive control, 9 cross-arm refusals and 6 real foreign artifacts correctly refused.
instrument_incidents: (1) NEW, generalisable: `kaggle kernels output` returned exit 0 while silently omitting both large logs (256KB kernel log, 360KB vLLM log); an identical re-pull minutes later retrieved them. Scored against the partial pull the scorer returned INFRA DEATH / 'served model absent' / cert_facts {} on a completely healthy run -- i.e. a download race nearly killed a certified arm. Tell: an instrument reporting a sick subject while reporting ZERO facts about it is describing itself. Mitigation: assert kernel-log presence and non-emptiness before scoring, and source certification facts from artifacts that survive partial pulls (here taaf_setup_env.json and prompts/*.log both arrived). (2) Separately re-confirmed on a third independent pull that a DIFFERENT arm's kernel log is genuinely 0 bytes while its sibling logs arrive intact -- a real capture defect, distinct from the partial-pull race.
sealed_reading_rule: prereg section 5: seed 1 alone certifies DELIVERY and NEVER produces an lc verdict (n=1 MDE 11.1). Failing D1, D2 or D3 with the arm ARMED => DELIVERY FAILURE, a distinct verdict class: not a null, not an infra death; licenses no statement about whether extra attempts buy levels; does not count against the prereg's kill budget; triggers re-scope, never re-read.
